content: I spend my whole life in going about, persuading you not to care for your bodies or your wealth, but first and foremost to care about the greatest improvement of the soul.
author: Socrates
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Reminding yourself of your mortality is not morbid; it is the most clarifying lens available to human consciousness. When you remember that your days are strictly numbered, petty resentments and trivial anxieties evaporate.

In Socrates's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Death gives urgency and sweetness to every ordinary afternoon. Because this day will never come again, the way you spend your attention right now is of monumental significance.
reflectionPrompt: In what area of your life are you overthinking the ideal approach instead of taking the simple, honorable action?
